vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: gws-gmail-reply
Version: 1.0.2

The skill bundle consists of documentation (SKILL.md) and metadata for an AI agent to interface with a Google Workspace CLI tool ('gws') to reply to Gmail messages. The instructions are consistent with the stated purpose, providing standard parameters for message IDs, bodies, and attachments, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection attacks.

llm.summary: The skill is a thin, instruction-only wrapper that delegates Gmail replies to a local 'gws' CLI; its requirements and instructions align with that purpose, but you should inspect the referenced shared SKILL.md and the gws binary before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Gmail reply) match the declared requirement of the 'gws' binary and the CLI usage in SKILL.md. Asking for the gws binary is appropriate for a CLI-based Gmail helper.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only documents invoking 'gws gmail +reply' and flags; it does not itself run arbitrary commands. However it explicitly directs the reader/agent to consult ../gws-shared/SKILL.md for auth, global flags, and security rules—so runtime behavior depends on that external shared file. Also the CLI supports attachments (file paths) which will cause local files to be read and transmitted when used.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files. Nothing is downloaded or written by this skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: This skill declares no required environment variables itself, which is reasonable because it delegates to the 'gws' CLI. But the referenced ../gws-shared/SKILL.md likely contains auth/global flags or environment requirements; you should review that file (or gws config) to see what credentials would actually be used.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent or cross-skill configuration changes. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal for skills) but not elevated here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a documentation/CLI wrapper that calls a local 'gws' program to send Gmail replies. Before installing or using it: 1) Confirm the 'gws' binary on your system is from a trusted source and inspect its permissions/behavior. 2) Open ../gws-shared/SKILL.md (the skill explicitly references it) to see how authentication is handled and whether any environment variables or tokens are required. 3) Be aware that using the --attach flag will read local files and upload them as email attachments. 4) If you cannot review the gws binary or the shared SKILL.md, treat this skill as higher risk and avoid granting it access to sensitive files or credentials.
